static_traits.name: Yang An
static_traits.social_status: Has Social support from friends and neighbors, but has not yet confided current troubles to them; relationship with spouse has become tense due to self-blame and irritability
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; without similar prior psychological problems or psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation, able to reflect on own thought patterns; obvious 'should' statements and self-criticism; initially tense but Positive attitude, willing to try reframing and practice

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling embarrassed and inadequate after failing to do one move in the most recent yoga class, repeatedly replaying the situation and developing thoughts of avoiding class again; also feeling Self-depreca because the corn is not growing as well as Anticipation
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to deal with the embarrassment and Self-doubt after yoga class, not letting these feelings dictate lifestyle and daily choices, and gaining a more balanced view through reality testing and thought reframing.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / incompetent
Only perfect performance shows I have worth

special_situations.event: In the last yoga class, failing to do one move while everyone else could do it
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do the move like others, it means I am not good enough and will be looked down on and ridiculed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding going to yoga class again to avoid embarrassment and others' evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I never want to go to yoga class again; everyone must think I am terrible

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking about attending the next yoga class or similar situations where failure may occur again
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail again, others will all notice and judge me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing and avoiding in advance, reducing exposure to situations where failure is possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely embarrass myself again; going will only make it more awkward

special_situations.event: Seeing the neighbor's crops yield a Good harvest while one's own corn grows poorly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my crops are not as good as the neighbor's, it proves I am a terrible Farmer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly switching fertilizers, asking others for advice while labeling oneself, being harsh on oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a terrible Farmer

special_situations.event: Finding poor growth when checking crops, associating it with one's own responsibility and performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should have known how to do it long ago and should not make mistakes, otherwise I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing oneself to improve through self-criticism and raising standards, while ignoring existing efforts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be better / I should have thought of this solution long ago

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, proving oneself to be a capable and worthy person
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being shamed for not being perfect or failing, being negated, appearing inferior to others after comparison
defense_goal: Reducing shame and the risk of being judged by avoiding situations that might expose inadequacy
Controlling Anxiety and maintaining a grip on self-worth through self-criticism and high standards

object_relations.self_representation: Oneself who is not good enough, prone to failure, disappointing others
object_relations.object_representation: Picky judges / others who succeed easily (classmates, neighbors)

object_relations.self_representation: A person who burdens the partner
object_relations.object_representation: A partner affected by one's own emotions who may be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing in counseling expressing one's own failures and feelings to others (friends, neighbors, or spouse)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying that others will see oneself as incompetent or be disappointed because of it
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Mainly self-blaming expressions (such as 'It is all my fault'), lowered tone, less emotional expression, avoiding directly expressing dissatisfaction and disappointment with others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Thinking of going to yoga class again or facing public occasions where she might fail
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will notice and ridicule one's inadequacy (others full of negative evaluations)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing worry about others' judgment implicitly, using vague language (such as 'everyone will think......'), reducing self-disclosure.

behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treating external standards as the sole basis of self-worth in an undigested way
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use normative, absolutist statements (such as 'I must, I should'), a harsh and restrained tone, fewer emotional words.

manifestations: Constraining oneself with rigid 'should/must' standards, unable to tolerate imperfection and mistakes
Choosing to avoid situations where failure is possible (such as not going to yoga class anymore), to reduce the risk of being judged
outcomes: Guilt and Increased anxiety, experiencing self-oppression and loss of Freedom to choose
Sleep impaired, Decreased drive, narrowed scope of life

manifestations: Knowing friends and neighbors are supportive, yet not confiding current troubles to them
Relationship with spouse grows distant due to self-blame and irritability
outcomes: Social support not yet activated, Increased subjective sense of isolation
Increased emotional burden, Negative self-evaluation persisting

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently has the self-demand 'I should/must be better'
Treats perfect performance as a necessary condition for self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: When facing unsatisfactory outcomes and comparisons, turning dissatisfaction and frustration into self-blame and self-attack
Not seeking help or expressing to others, instead repressing emotions, bearing it alone

positive_force: Has genuine interest and investment in activities such as yoga, and long enjoyed the classes
Has a tendency to seek help and try to improve (changing fertilizer, asking neighbors for advice)
Has some awareness of cognitive distortions, willing to do reality testing and restructuring
Having available social support resources (friends, neighbors, spouse)
Positive attitude toward counseling, with a sense of hope and action plans (recording restructuring, gratitude practice)
negative_force: Perfectionism and rigid 'should' rules dominate self-evaluation
Cognitive patterns of overgeneralization, mental filtering, and negating the positive
Sensitive to social comparison, relies on external evaluation to confirm self-worth
Avoiding potentially failing situations (such as not going to yoga class anymore), leading to limited experiences and abilities
Self-blame and guilt worsen the emotional burden, affecting sleep and relationships

antecedent: Thinking about attending the next yoga class
Recalling the last time in class when one could not do the move but others could
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic Anticipation of failure/embarrassment under perfectionist standards and Fear of others' judgment
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome things (shame and being judged), temporarily lowering Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Weekly routines disrupted, fewer interest activities, Negative emotions persisting and reinforcing Self-doubt

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-criticism and 'should'-style self-blame (such as 'I should be better/I should have known earlier')
antecedent: Finding poor growth when checking crops
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting external standards as the basis for judging self-worth, and equating losses with 'I am not good enough' in social comparison
target_behavior.function: Obtaining a sense of control and self-drive through self-attack, trying to avoid facing vulnerability and the need to seek help
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, Relationship tension with spouse, Sleep difficulties, decreased Work drive
